content.comment_body: I'm encountering the same issue as [user_name]. Even after enabling the web user, I still see the [company_name] Third-Party Software Disclosure Document when entering the IP address.
This indicates that the web server is not fully activated. When you enabled the web user, did you set a password and then click "Apply"?
Consider starting a support request for further assistance.

Hello, if you only see the [company_name] Third-Party Software Disclosure Document, the web server is not enabled. That screen only provides open-source software (OSS) information. Go to [product_name] configuration, find Tools/Access control, and enable the web server while specifying a password. Make sure you are using the correct version of [product_name]. After making these changes, try to connect again.

Hello, you might also try using a different web browser. In my case, Google Chrome displayed the same "[company_name] Third-Party Software Disclosure Document..." message. When I switched to Microsoft Edge, it worked properly. Best regards!

analysis.insight_summary: Users face confusion trying to access the web server on [product_name] and instead see a '[company_name] Third-Party Software Disclosure Document' rather than the expected web interface. Uncertainty remains about proper web server activation and browser compatibility. Troubleshooting steps, including password setup and browser switching, are discussed, but at least one user still experiences the problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that enabling the web user and configuring a password should grant seamless access to the [product_name] web server and its visualization interface via a browser.
